pins.title: Slow right down
pins.sub: The air is thinner up high. Take smaller steps, rest more often, drink water, and head back down if a headache gets worse.

pins.title: Plan a free park day
items: Entrance fees waived for US residents
Camping and tours still cost extra
pins.sub: Planning the Smokies, Utah or Yellowstone? One set of guides for all three.

pins.kicker: Taking your dog to a national park?
pins.title: Check the trail rules
pins.sub: In most national parks dogs can't go on most trails. Check the park's pets page before you drive.

pins.title: Fit it at home
pins.sub: Try it on your own boots before the trip: toe in first, stretch it over the heel, chains flat under the sole. Check again after a mile.

pins.title: Cut the extras
items: Food for the night, not a week
Refill and treat water at camp
pins.sub: Weigh your pack at home and take out what you didn't use last trip.

pins.title: Scoop, then filter
pins.sub: Fill a soft bottle where the water runs, then drink through the filter straw. Pick clear, moving water when you can.

pins.kicker: Sweaty on the climb, cold at the top?
pins.title: Start a bit cold
pins.sub: Start with fewer layers than feels comfy, unzip before you sweat, and pull on a warm layer the moment you stop.

pins.title: Plan 2027 now
pins.sub: A printable year planner with a hike-a-week challenge: pick your trails now and tick them off all year.

pins.title: Free on Nov 11
pins.sub: Entrance is free for US residents on Veterans Day. High roads like Trail Ridge Road close for winter, so check road status on nps.gov first.

pins.kicker: Hiking alone for the first time?
pins.title: Leave a plan
pins.sub: Tell someone your trail, your start time and when to call for help. Pick a busy, marked trail and turn back early if the weather turns.
